Equal keys hash equally with Hashtbl.hash and immutable strings/variants. Http and Http_unobserved still share HTTP transport; Official_client remains separate even with identical slot text. assessments.topic: Slot order, duplicate declarations and declared flag
assessments.reason: All declared HTTP keys are inserted first, then declared CLI, then matching historical rows in original runs/observation order. A separate reverse first-insertion list, never table iteration, determines output. Existing entries are not appended or overwritten. Thus duplicates retain their first position, declaration=true survives later historical hits, and truly historical-only entries remain false.

List.iter over runs and List.iteri over the original complete observation list retain original per-run index even when another owner is excluded. Cons then List.rev per group reconstructs exactly the old retained-list filter order. Unchanged latest chooses maximum(time,run_id,index) with strict >, so complete equal anchors keep the earlier occurrence exactly as before. Undated outcomes preserve original run/list order without borrowing run.started_at.

Filtering remains observation.lane_key=Some(exact_lane_key owner), not inferred from logical run.lane. None and Some(Error _) are still skipped; Some(Ok[]) and observations for another/missing owner add nothing. Current declarations/bindings cannot supply historical endpoint or time. Caller unavailable-observation accounting is separate and unchanged. Historical observed_json still encodes the exact selected original observation.

The entire latest helper and four last_* predicates, started/finished fallback and outcome constructors are unchanged. Success/failure still require observed finish, unresolved undated rows stay out, undated resolved outcomes remain separately listed. Finite-date validation remains the observation API contract; the refactor introduces no time parser/default or new float comparator.

Current binding index inserts only when absent, matching original List.assoc_opt first string-key match including duplicates. Only HTTP rows use it; CLI current_binding is still null. Values remain actual typed binding observations and output field ordering/encoding is unchanged.

When declarations and runs are all empty, original slots is empty independently of current_http; direct [] result is equivalent. exact_lane_key is pure typed owner-to-string construction, so skipping it adds no observable authority/error normalization. This is only the strict empty triple fastpath, not a claim that every filtered-empty input has zero work.

Both table instances, first-seen list and mutable group records are constructed inside one call. Functor module contains implementation code, no global table/cache. Only newly allocated group list fields mutate; inputs are read-only. Returned Yojson contains no table, group ref or callback. Matching observations temporarily retain run references as baseline retained tuples did; new buckets/records/reverse copies add metadata and no live/peak heap benefit is proved. Concurrent calls share no grouping state.

Existing endpoint/history assertions remain; duplicate current binding proves first wins and duplicate declarations dedupe per transport. Added HTTP/CLI H rows check declared-first/historical-first-seen order, false historical declaration, run-id and observation-index tie ordering across last_observation/attempt/success, separate failure and original undated run order. It uses actual existing observation constructors/decoder and slot projector, no fake interface or new dependency/API. This is source inspection only; no executed test result yet.

complexity.definitions: R runs; O all observed rows inspected; M owner-matching rows; D declarations incl duplicates; C current binding entries; G distinct matching transport/slot keys. Include string hashing/equality and JSON output-byte costs.
complexity.candidate: With ordinary hash distribution and amortized table resize, O(R+O+D+C+G) grouping/index/order work plus constant passes over total M and output serialization/key bytes. It removes repeated per-slot scans of all M retained rows and repeated linear uniqueness/declaration/current-binding lookup.
complexity.baseline: List.mem plus append uniqueness and per-group history/filter/current lookups can cost O((D+M)*G + G*(M+D+C)) before output.
complexity.limits: Hashtbl.Make is non-seeded under actual OCaml interface; adversarial collisions or long string keys can make operations slower. No guaranteed worst-case linear claim. The new current index always scans C in a non-fastpath call, even if runs yield zero matching groups; tiny/filtered-empty/one-hot inputs can pay extra setup. Allocation/CPU tradeoffs need actual bounded evidence; no universal speedup implied.
